correctness.rationale: For every integer r>=1, the proposed projection is an explicit convex combination of symmetric permutation matrices. For any involution, the exact Frobenius residual pairing depends only on its counts I of internal transpositions, C of cross-triple transpositions and F of fixed points. The bounds I<=r, F+2(I+C)=3r, and F>=1 when r is odd yield a universal supporting-hyperplane inequality, attained by every involution in the constructed mixture. The necessary-and-sufficient Euclidean projection criterion and strict convexity establish unique optimality, including r=1. Direct entry counting yields both rational norm formulas. An actual standalone checker verifies exact rational identities through r=25 and exhaustively enumerates involutions through r=4; numerical QPs through r=3 are independent corroboration, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A half-weighted triangle is the smallest fractional extreme block of the symmetric doubly stochastic polytope, and repeating it gives a canonical arbitrary-size test of integral matching approximation. The exact Frobenius projection shows that cross-block transpositions reduce squared loss asymptotically from r/2 under independent rounding to r/6, and detects a sharp even/odd fixed-point correction through an explicit unique minimizing matrix. This gives a motivated natural geometric invariant with a meaningful exact structural and asymptotic interpretation; it does not claim a full Hausdorff theorem.
